description: Question: silicon, GaAs, GaN, ZnSe, SiC: why is every semiconductor in a chip built of atoms with exactly four neighbours, while table salt and magnesium oxide, made of the same kinds of elements, take six? Data: every stable binary AB compound in Alexandria (PBE ground states, keyless OPTIMADE) with 2 or 4 atoms per cell made of main-group and d10 elements, and PubChem's periodic table for valence electrons, electronegativity and period. Steps: keep the octet compounds (two atoms bringing 8 valence electrons: I-VII, II-VI, III-V, IV-IV); read the coordination from the ground-state space group (zincblende and wurtzite 4, rock salt 6, CsCl 8); place each on the Mooser–Pearson map (Pauling electronegativity difference Δχ against the mean principal quantum number n̄); find the best single Δχ threshold and Fisher's linear discriminant on both, and their accuracy against always guessing the larger class. Aha: the structure is predictable from two atomic numbers: covalent bonds between light atoms (small Δχ, small n̄) are directional sp³ bonds pointing to four neighbours, the open tetrahedral network that gives a band gap with mobile carriers; ionic bonds (large Δχ) are not directional and pack six neighbours. One number already does most of the work: Δχ below about 1.3 predicts four neighbours for 87% of the compounds (against 52% for always guessing the larger class), and adding n̄ (Fisher's line) gets 91%. ZnO and BeO stay tetrahedral at quite large Δχ because their atoms are small, MgO and CdO go rock salt. Caveats: Pauling's Δχ is a crude ionicity (Phillips' spectroscopic ionicity from optical data separates the two classes completely at 0.785, but needs dielectric constants not fetched here); ground states are PBE at zero temperature and pressure (energy differences of a few meV/atom can flip: PBE puts LiCl, LiBr and LiI in wurtzite, while they crystallise as rock salt, and those three are most of the line's misses); no IV-IV compound (SiC) is in the ground-state set with these cell sizes; compounds with larger cells are left out; the discriminant is fitted and judged on the same compounds. Next: drill into the misclassified compounds (scored table), expand to Phillips ionicity with dielectric data, or to how pressure turns tetrahedral semiconductors into rock salt.
name: Why semiconductors are tetrahedral: the Mooser–Pearson map
